language.script: Hebrew (with Arabic and Latin on many signs)
language.script_notes: Hebrew letters — read right to left and mostly square and blocky — stand out at once and appear across the country; road signs are usually shown in Hebrew, Arabic and English together. Arabic script appears alone or alongside Hebrew in Arab towns and villages. The internet domain is .il.

road_furniture.curb_style: Kerbs and the bases of poles are painted black and white; kerbs can also alternate yellow and red, or white and red — a strong tell.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Tower-like utility structures are common in cities.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs crowded with rooftop solar water heaters and water tanks — rooftop solar collectors supply hot water to about 80% of households.
architecture.wall_construction: White Bauhaus-style buildings in Tel Aviv's 'White City', painted white to reflect the sun; local Jerusalem limestone as the building stone of the capital; concrete apartment blocks in most towns.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Bauhaus and International-style apartment blocks with curved balconies; Jerusalem-stone buildings; rooftops covered in solar water heaters; kibbutz and moshav villages; ancient walls and ruins.

nature.vegetation: Mediterranean scrub, olive and pine in the rainy north, citrus groves on the coastal plain, and sparse desert and steppe vegetation in the south.
nature.terrain: A small country of great contrasts — a Mediterranean coastal plain, the hills around Jerusalem and Galilee, the Jordan Rift Valley and Dead Sea, and the arid Negev desert covering the south.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean with winter rain in the north, and hot, dry desert in the south.

vehicles.plate_color: Yellow plates with black text — the main plate tell, shared in Europe only with the Netherlands and Luxembourg; Palestinian-registered vehicles have green or white plates.
vehicles.plate_format: Numerals separated by hyphens (two digits, three digits, two digits), in black on yellow.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: The national hiking trail, running from the northernmost point to the southern tip, is covered by trekker imagery.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring landscapes, Arabic-script towns and similar terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Yellow plates and the black-and-white painted kerbs and pole bases are the reliable tells here; Palestinian-registered vehicles carry green or white plates.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Levantine landscape, Arabic script and stone architecture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Hebrew signs, yellow plates and rooftop solar water heaters point here; Jordan and Lebanon use Arabic-first signage and different plates.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Sinai and Negev desert terrain along the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Hebrew signs and yellow plates versus Arabic signs and Egyptian plates.
